clue.text: Send friendly message with well-penned substance, perhaps

parts.note: ink is held in an inkwell and flows from a pen, so it is a substance kept in a well and penned

explanation.surface: Someone signs off a cheery note written with a fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-penned' reads as 'nicely written', but it means held in an inkwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing one eye at someone is a wordless signal of friendliness or shared understanding.

clue.text: Something Kipling wrote to some extent describes Tanzania

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Kipling's writing about East Africa partly describes Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling was a poet, and a verse unit of a poem is something he would have written.

clue.text: Pervert portrayed as exploitative

indicators.note: to pervert something is to twist it out of its proper form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sexual deviant is depicted as someone who takes advantage of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun, a person being portrayed, but it is a verb telling you to scramble PORTRAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preys on others exploits them, so a preying manner is an exploitative one.

clue.text: Respected guide meets excursion group going back inside

indicators.note: going back means the hidden run is read from right to left
inside says the letters sit within the run of words guide, meets, excursion

explanation.surface: A tour guide joins a party of day-trippers heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DEMEETSE spans 'guiDE MEETS Excursion'; read backwards it gives the answer. 'group' is only a link word filling out the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held in high regard is to be respected; the two are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Obsolete cars take the road in Italy to reach former republic

parts.note: the Yugo was a cheap small car, no longer made
in Italian, la via means the road

explanation.surface: Old bangers drive along an Italian road to get to an ex-communist state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yugo was a notoriously poor-quality car built there, the butt of many jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balkan federation broke up in the 1990s, making it a republic that no longer exists.

clue.text: Orient, possibly, at the outset after clarifying advice

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letter of the word possibly and also puts it at the front
after clarifying suggests the word Orient has been sorted out, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is told to head east after getting clearer instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' looks like the definition but is the anagram fodder; the definition is 'advice' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a useful hint or tip, a piece of guidance on what to do.

clue.text: Church submits before uprising

indicators.note: before says the word for submits comes ahead of the church abbreviation

parts.note: to submit a proposal is to put it forward

explanation.surface: The church gives in ahead of a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent attempt to seize government is a kind of revolt or rising.

clue.text: Greet us clumsily and wave

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the words Greet us are handled awkwardly and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to us awkwardly and waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the hand is a typical example of a meaningful movement of the body.

clue.text: Burden of testing periodically brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
periodically takes letters at regular intervals from the word testing

explanation.surface: The weight of being examined now and then is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of testing give TSIG, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The burden of an argument is its main point, the same sense as its essence or core.

clue.text: Place in vault with space to add doctor

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical qualification standing for doctor

explanation.surface: A burial vault is laid out with room for a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The en is a typesetting space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a body in a tomb or crypt is to bury it there.

clue.text: Jack's predecessor receiving endorsement of minimal value

indicators.note: receiving says the card takes the approval word inside it

parts.note: in a suit of cards the ten comes just before the jack
to give something the OK is to approve or endorse it

explanation.surface: A man called Jack's predecessor in a job gets a lukewarm reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a person, but it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture done only for show is nominal and of slight worth, as in a token payment.

clue.text: Served, did she?

parts.note: take the first word of the entry and put it out, that is jumble it, and its letters give did she

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether she was the one who waited at table.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the second word, 'out', is the anagram signal working on the first, which rearranges to give 'did she'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is served when it is ladled onto plates, the phrasal verb meaning distributed portions.

clue.text: Creative hairstyling, you might say, in stock pictures

definitions.meaning: the skill of cutting hair with clippers, jokingly called an art
ready-made images supplied for pasting into documents

explanation.surface: An inventive hairdresser's work appears in a library of images.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a whimsical reading of the phrase as an art of clipping hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made graphics sold or bundled for inserting into documents are known by this computing term.

clue.text: Where you might find sandwiches etc a disaster, lacking in taste

parts.note: sandwiches are sold in a delicatessen, so you find them in a deli

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the letters of etc a are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sandwich shop's lunch spread is a disaster and tastes bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in taste' suggests flavour, but it means vulgar or improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude or coarse shows a lack of good taste or tact.

clue.text: Characteristic image of returning setter (me) pocketing pound

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembly is read backwards
pocketing says the pound abbreviation goes inside the pair of me words

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler pockets cash and returns with a picture of themself.
explanation.walkthrough: ME, LB, ME makes MELBME, which reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge or symbol that stands for something is a representative image of it.

clue.text: Absurd poeticisms initially rejected in study of communication

indicators.note: absurd suggests the remaining letters are put into a nonsensical new order
initially rejected means the opening letter of poeticisms is thrown out

explanation.surface: Silly poetic phrases are turned down at the first attempt in language studies.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping P leaves OETICISMS, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This academic discipline examines signs and symbols and how they convey meaning.

clue.text: Basic desire for one belief

parts.note: in Freudian psychology the id is the part of the mind holding instinctive desires
EA, short for each, means for one, as in a price per item

explanation.surface: A primal urge supplies one person's conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion or notion someone holds is a thought they believe in.

clue.text: Elements of type found within spermatozoa

parts.note: the letters A, TO and Z sit inside the word spermatozoa, spelling the full range of letters

explanation.surface: A biology note about something contained in sperm cells.
explanation.walkthrough: SpermATOZoa holds A TO Z, everything from the first letter to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters are the basic units of printed type, and the complete set of them runs from A to Z.

clue.text: Sounding slightly twisted in spirit

indicators.note: sounding says the word for slightly twisted is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a wry smile or neck is bent a little to one side

explanation.surface: Someone sounds a little warped in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like mood, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky distilled from a cereal grain is a kind of spirit, especially in North America.

clue.text: Pacifist in America jumped off cliff

definitions.meaning: a peace-loving politician, the opposite of a hawk
the American past tense of dive, where British English says dived

explanation.surface: A peace campaigner in the US leapt from a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird symbolising peace names those who oppose war; Americans also use it as the past tense of dive.

clue.text: Invent what uranium and phosphorus do in combination

definitions.meaning: to invent a story is to concoct it

definitions.text: what uranium and phosphorus do in combination
definitions.meaning: the chemical symbols U and P together form a little word, so they constitute it

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about how two elements combine to create something new.
explanation.walkthrough: U is uranium and P phosphorus; put together they spell UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventing an excuse is fabricating it; the phrasal verb means to concoct.

clue.text: Mark hurls after eating my turnover

indicators.note: turnover means the result is flipped and read backwards
after eating says the throwing word has swallowed the word my

parts.note: to lob is to throw or hurl

explanation.surface: A man named Mark throws up after eating my pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name and 'turnover' like a pastry; one is the definition and the other means the whole thing is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or character standing for something, such as a punctuation mark, is a symbol.

clue.text: Inclined to be half asleep, Pontiff stripped of original power

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters of asleep
stripped of original says the first occurrence of the power letter is removed

parts.note: the Pontiff is the Pope
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A drowsy Pope, robbed of his authority, is inclined to doze.
explanation.walkthrough: ASL plus OPE. 'Inclined' looks like 'disposed to', but it means sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a slant or slope is tilted, which is one sense of inclined.

clue.text: Is love gay, embracing male in a form of sexual union?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

indicators.note: embracing says the word gay wraps around the male abbreviation

explanation.surface: A question about whether love between men counts as a kind of union.
explanation.walkthrough: IS, O and GA(M)Y combine.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology this term names fusion of reproductive cells that are alike in size and form.

clue.text: Slow vehicle from old times superior to, say, Tesla model

indicators.note: superior to in a down clue means the earlier pieces are placed above the rest

parts.note: the multiplication sign x is read as times
a Tesla is an example of a car, as say signals
the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model leads to T

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned vehicle is claimed to be better than a modern electric car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior to' looks like 'better than', but in a down clue it means 'placed above'.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm wagon drawn by bullocks is a notoriously slow form of transport.

clue.text: Asking in every other place for hint

indicators.note: every other place takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the words Asking in

explanation.surface: Someone asks around in various places for a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication or trace of something, such as a sign of rain, is a hint of it.

clue.text: Curate and his unconventional liturgy

indicators.note: unconventional suggests the letters of Curate and his are arranged in a non-standard way

explanation.surface: A clergyman's assistant conducts an unusual church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Communion is the central Christian service, a liturgy of bread and wine.

clue.text: Reached peak, got rid of unnecessary baggage, beginning ascent

indicators.note: unnecessary says the word for got rid of is surplus and is dropped

parts.note: to reach a peak or high point is to climax
to axe something is to get rid of it

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word baggage

explanation.surface: A mountaineer reached the summit after shedding excess luggage at the start of the climb.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIMAXED loses AXED to leave CLIM, then B from baggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up a slope or mountain is an act of ascending; the noun names that upward progress.

clue.text: Half-eaten taco filling in recycle bin?

indicators.note: filling says what is left of the taco goes inside the word in
half-eaten means the first half of the word taco has been consumed and removed

explanation.surface: A partly eaten taco is thrown into the recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: TACO minus TA leaves CO, placed inside IN. 'bin' is a computer desktop symbol, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer desktop, the waste-basket picture is an example of a small clickable graphic.

clue.text: Fast-talking Nationalist's plan

parts.note: patter is the glib rapid talk of a salesman or comedian

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking nationalist politician sets out his scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A design or template to be followed is a model or plan for making something.

clue.text: Average for a golfer? That's fine, according to Spooner, but practise driving with colleagues

indicators.note: according to Spooner says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: par is the standard score expected of a good golfer on a hole
cool is an informal way of saying that is fine

explanation.surface: A golfer hears that a middling score is fine, then gets told to share lifts to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of PAR COOL gives CAR POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing lifts to work, taking turns behind the wheel, is the verb's meaning.
